facts.statement: Neuquenraptor is estimated to have been between 1.8 and 3.5 meters long and weighed 75 kilograms.
facts.quote: Neuquenraptor is estimated to have measured 1.8 - 3.5 m long and have weighed 75 kg.

facts.statement: Neuquenraptor was larger than its close relative Buitreraptor, with which it shared some osteological and physical similarities.
facts.quote: Era más grande que su pariente cercano Buitreraptor, un género con el que compartía algunas similitudes osteológicas y físicas.

facts.statement: Neuquenraptor was an active predator with long arms and legs, a long and curved skull, sharp claws and teeth, and a slender, graceful body.
facts.quote: Fue un depredador activo que poseía brazos y piernas largas, un cráneo alargado y curvo, garras y dientes afilados, sumado a un cuerpo delgado y grácil.

facts.statement: Although little is known about the appearance of Neuquenraptor argentinus, characteristic crescent-shaped claws are present in the fossil.
facts.quote: Poco se sabe sobre el aspecto de Neuquenraptor argentinus, pero las garras características en forma de media luna están presentes en el fósil.

facts.statement: Neuquenraptor was approximately the same size as Velociraptor and likely had feathers like it.
facts.quote: Neuquenraptor era aproximadamente del mismo tamaño que Velociraptor y probablemente también tenía plumas como este.

facts.statement: The remains of Neuquenraptor were found near Plaza Huincul in the Sierra del Portezuelo in January 1996 and reported that same year.
facts.quote: In January 1996 the remains of Neuquenraptor were found near Plaza Huincul in the Sierra del Portezuelo and reported that very year.

facts.statement: Neuquenraptor argentinus was formally named and described as a dromaeosaurid in 2005 by Fernando Novas and Diego Pol.
facts.quote: However, it was named as the type species Neuquenraptor argentinus in 2005 by Fernando Novas of the Bernardino Rivadavia Natural Sciences Museum and Diego Pol of Ohio State University and described as a dromaeosaurid.

facts.statement: The known remains, holotype MCF-PVPH 77, were discovered in layers of the Portezuelo Formation dating to the Coniacian.
facts.quote: Los restos conocidos, holotipo MCF-PVPH 77, fueron descubiertos en capas de la Formación Portezuelo que datan del Coniaciano.

facts.statement: The known fossil material consists only of a left foot, some cervical vertebrae fragments, ribs, tail chevrons, and a radius.
facts.quote: Se compone solo de un pie izquierdo, algunos fragmentos de vértebras cervicales, costillas, galones de cola y un radio.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Neuquenraptor is a junior subjective synonym of Unenlagia, as the latter name was published earlier in 1997 and has priority.
facts.quote: Neuquenraptor might be a junior subjective synonym of Unenlagia; that is, the two might represent the same genus or even species, in which case the name Unenlagia would have to be used instead of Neuquenraptor because the former name was published earlier, in 1997, and thus has priority.

facts.statement: Neuquenraptor lived from the Turonian to the Coniacian, approximately 93.9 to 85.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Coniacian (93.9 to 85.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: Before Neuquenraptor's discovery, all dromaeosaurids were known from the Northern Hemisphere, leading scientists to believe the group only inhabited Laurasia.
facts.quote: Until the discovery of Neuquenraptor, all dromaeosaurids had been found in North America, Europe or Northern China / Mongolia, and scientists believed that dromaeosaurids only inhabited Laurasia, i.e. the Northern Hemisphere.

facts.statement: The discovery of Neuquenraptor provides possible evidence regarding the degree of isolation between the Northern and Southern hemispheres during the Mesozoic.
facts.quote: The find of Neuquenraptor provides some possible indication of the degree of isolation between the Northern and Southern hemispheres.

facts.statement: Researchers have attempted to synonymize Neuquenraptor with Unenlagia, but some published analyses suggest Unenlagia is more basal.
facts.quote: Se lo ha intentado sinonimizar con Unenlagia, pero este último, aunque de los mismos niveles, resulta ser más basal en algunos análisis publicados.

rejected.statement: Neuquenraptor is a genus of unenlagiine theropod dinosaurs that lived in the Late Cretaceous in the Portezuelo Formation of Argentina.
rejected.quote: Neuquenraptor (meaning Neuquén thief) is a genus of unenlagiine theropod dinosaurs that lived in South America during the Late Cretaceous in what is now the Portezuelo Formation of Argentina.
